title: Hardware Implementation of Blind Decoding of Downlink Control Information for 5G
problem: 5G user equipment (UE) must blindly decode Downlink Control Information (DCI) from multiple candidate locations within 0.25 ms stringent time limit. Exhaustive search across candidates is computationally intensive and imposes significant latency, risking missed decoding deadlines.
motivation: 5G NR (new radio) standard requires blind decoding of DCIs to discover time-frequency resource allocations, modulation, and coding without prior signaling. The search space can exceed 40+ candidates. Hardware acceleration is necessary to meet the 0.25 ms latency budget on resource-constrained UE devices.
method: The system tests different possible interpretations of an incoming signal across multiple candidate locations to find which one contains the needed control information (blind decoding). Rather than checking each possibility in software—which would be too slow—they built dedicated hardware using a Xilinx Zynq Ultrascale+ RFSoC ZCU111 FPGA board to test multiple candidates in parallel, guaranteeing results within 0.25 milliseconds. The hardware was integrated into an existing 5G receiver and validated using a real 5G testbed.
key_novelty: An FPGA-based decoder that performs blind DCI decoding in 0.25 milliseconds while using only 65% of the hardware's available computational resources.
contributions: Flexible hardware implementation for 5G DCI blind decoding
Achieves 0.25 ms latency budget with 65% time utilization
Integrated into existing 5G testbed UE receive chain
Validated on Xilinx Zynq Ultrascale+ RFSoC (ZCU111)
Demonstrated functionality and performance on real 5G testbed
limitations: Abstract only; detailed architecture and optimization techniques not disclosed; latency breakdown (search vs. decoding vs. CRC) not provided; power consumption not characterized; scalability to different search space sizes not discussed; comparison with software implementations or other hardware approaches missing; memory requirements and bandwidth not specified; support for dynamic DCI format adaptation not mentioned.
